answer: A sybil farm must replicate the full bond per fake identity, so costs rise linearly while rewards stay flat. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent locks collateral at registration, and voting power scales with bonded stake, not headcount. Reputation accrues along a trust ridge: legitimate peers climb toward the zenith, while fresh clones sit at the base. Any verified contribution leaves a signed plume in the ledger, making duplicate personas detectable and slashable. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
